prose.root_cause: Extension and Leaf matching in verify() compares nibbles one by one but never validates the remaining nibble count: Leaf matching succeeds when the input key ends even with node nibbles left over, Extension matching stops at the first mismatch and its little-endian padding zeros are indistinguishable from real zeros.
prose.summary: CairoLib's MPT verifier (verify(key, key_len, proof)) matches Extension and Leaf node nibbles without checking how many nibbles remain, so a truncated key or a forged key that skips an Extension node can be verified against someone else's proof (CS-HRDTCL-005, Critical).
prose.title: CairoLib MPT verify accepts partial and forged keys because nibble length is never validated

prose.root_cause: bytes_used_u64 computes how many bytes of the last Words64 item are significant from the value itself, which cannot distinguish leading zero bytes from unused padding, so trailing zeros of the big-endian input are omitted and the digest differs from keccak of the intended input.

affected_components: Cetus CLMM clmm_math::get_delta_a (the caller both analyses identify)
input.prompt: Which language and which ecosystem does this finding concern? Answer {"language": ..., "ecosystem": ...} using the dataset's own vocabulary.

prose.root_cause: checked_shlw computes mask = 0xffffffffffffffff << 192 and tests n > mask, which is not the intended n >= 1 << 192 test, so most values greater than 2^192 pass; the subsequent << 64 then wraps silently (Move shifts do not abort), and clmm_math::get_delta_a divides the truncated numerator by p0*p1 and casts the result to u64
prose.summary: checked_shlw was meant to detect that a u256 overflows when shifted left by 64 bits, but tested against 0xffffffffffffffff << 192 instead of 1 << 192, so values above 2^192 passed undetected; the 320-bit product produced by get_delta_a then wrapped inside the u256 and collapsed to a tiny residue, so the token-A deposit for a liquidity add was computed as almost nothing while the LP tokens minted were not, and repeated add/remove cycles drained the pool on 2025-05-22.
prose.title: A wrong overflow mask in math_u256::checked_shlw silently truncated a 320-bit product, letting an attacker mint unbacked liquidity and drain the Cetus CLMM on 2025-05-22

prose.root_cause: instruction decoding and verify_secure_runner in the RustVM lacked validation that the AIR requires (for a call instruction the fixed flags dst_register == AP, dst_offset == 0, op0_register == AP, op0_offset == 1, ap_update == Add2, fp_update == APPlus2 are checkable), so a decoded instruction could run on the sequencer while being unsatisfiable for the prover.

prose.title: Cairo VM sequencer-prover inconsistency: a program can execute on the RustVM while violating the prover's AIR

prose.root_cause: Value depth enforcement in the Move VM was insufficient, so deeply nested values could drive the interpreter/loader past a safe stack depth
prose.summary: The Move VM accepted values whose nesting depth exceeded what the VM can safely walk, so a crafted value could overflow the VM stack; Aptos landed commit 47a0391c 'cherry-pick: improved value depth checks in the VM (#8488)' on 2023-06-02, and NVD lists that commit as a patch for CVE-2023-36184.
prose.title: Deeply nested values could overflow the Move VM stack; Aptos hardened value depth checks in commit 47a0391c

prose.root_cause: the callback validated order_id alone rather than the whole receipt/order binding, so a payment could be made to an unintended target while the assertion still passed
prose.summary: The flash-loan callback checked only that order_id matched the object id, so an attacker could route a payment elsewhere while satisfying the check; OpenZeppelin prints the fix as an added `assert!(order_id == object::id(limit_order), EMismatchedOrder)`.
prose.title: OpenZeppelin: Cetus flash-loan callback validated only order_id instead of the full receipt, allowing a misrouted payment to steal funds
